short: The Red Army's breakthrough heavy tank, built around a 122 mm gun.
full:
Adopted on 31 October 1943, the IS-2 replaced the IS-1 after its 85 mm gun proved insufficient. Its 122 mm D-25T fired a 25 kg shell that could wreck a bunker or blow the turret off a Panther, at the price of separate-loading ammunition, a rate of fire of two or three rounds a minute, and only 28 rounds carried. It first fought in April 1944 with the 11th and 72nd Independent Guards Heavy Tank Regiments.

It was never meant to hunt tanks. Guards heavy tank regiments were breakthrough troops, sent to crack fortified lines and support assaults, and the IS-2 led the street fighting in Berlin in 1945. Around 3,400 were built. The T-10 took over the front-line heavy role in the 1950s, but modernised IS-2Ms remained in Soviet inventory in reserve and fixed defences for decades, taking part in exercises as late as 1982 and only being formally struck off in 1995.
